say.en: A company says its "average salary" is 80,000 rupees. Most workers earn 25,000, rupees but the CEO earns 50 rupees lakh. Which average is the company using? In this lesson: State the relation Mode equals 3 Median minus 2 Mean.
Compare the three averages and choose the right one.

body.en: In a symmetrical distribution, mean = median = mode. In a moderately skewed distribution, Karl Pearson's *empirical relation* holds: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean. In a positively skewed distribution mean > median > mode; in a negatively skewed one mean < median < mode. The median always lies between the mean and the mode.
body.kn: ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಾಸರಿ = ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ = ಬಹುಲಕ. ಮಧ್ಯಮ ಓರೆಯ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಹುಲಕ = 3 ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ − 2 ಸರಾಸರಿ. ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಬಹುಲಕದ ನಡುವೆ.

say.en: In a symmetrical distribution, mean equals median equals mode. In a moderately skewed distribution, Karl Pearson's empirical relation holds: Mode equals 3 Median minus 2 Mean. In a positively skewed distribution mean is greater than median is greater than mode; in a negatively skewed one mean is less than median is less than mode. The median always lies between the mean and the mode. Symmetrical: Mean equals Median equals Mode.
say.kn: ಸಮಮಿತೀಯ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸರಾಸರಿ = ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ equals ಬಹುಲಕ. ಮಧ್ಯಮ ಓರೆಯ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬಹುಲಕ equals 3 ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ minus 2 ಸರಾಸರಿ. ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಮತ್ತು ಬಹುಲಕದ ನಡುವೆ.

title.en: On the board: Where the three averages sit

say.en: In a symmetric distribution mean, median and mode are equal.
With a long tail to the right, the distribution is positively skewed.
The mean is pulled furthest into the tail, the mode stays at the peak, the median sits between.
For moderate skew: mode equals three medians minus two means.
On the board: Where the three averages sit.

title.en: Mean, median and mode in skewed data

caption.en: Change the skewness. In a symmetrical curve all three coincide. With a long right tail (positive skew) mean > median > mode; flip it for negative skew. Check Pearson's rule: mode ≈ 3 median − 2 mean.

body.en: The mean uses all values and suits further calculation but is pulled by extremes. The *median* suits skewed data like incomes and open-ended classes. The mode suits the most common item, like a size, and qualitative data.

steps.en: So the distribution is slightly negatively skewed.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. In a moderately skewed distribution, mean = 25.5 and median = 25.83. Estimate the mode and state the type of skewness.

say.en: Let us work this out together. In a moderately skewed distribution, mean equals 25.5 and median equals 25.83. Estimate the mode and state the type of skewness.
Mode equals 3 times 25.83 minus 2 times 25.5 equals 77.49 minus 51 equals 26.49 about 26.5.
Here mean is less than median is less than mode.
So the distribution is slightly negatively skewed.
So the answer is Mode is approximately 26.5; slightly negatively skewed.

body.en: For a positive (right) skew, the averages from largest to smallest are in alphabetical order: Mean > Median > Mode, because the mean is pulled furthest into the tail. For a negative skew, simply reverse the order.
